props.name: container
props.description: Portal target for the country picker. Defaults to the nearest enclosing `ThemeScope` element.

props.name: countries
props.description: The countries the picker offers, as ISO codes. The metadata still parses every number: detection only selects a listed country, so a number from another one stays in international form beside the selected country, as with trimmed metadata. With one country the field shows its flag and dial code as plain context instead of a picker. Codes outside the catalog, without a packaged flag or in the product exclusions are ignored, and a list that leaves no country throws. A change that drops the selected country keeps the shown number's international identity, except a controlled `raw` value, which names no country and reads again in the one that remains. The rows sort by name whatever the list's order.

props.name: countryCode
props.description: Authoritative controlled country, paired with `onCountryChange`; it wins over `defaultCountryCode`. The field shows, in order: the country a controlled `value` names, else a proposal's country the parent holds, else `countryCode` as the picker resolves it. A controlled `value` names a country when its own `+` or `00` prefix detects an offered country, with `autoDetectCountry` on; a partial number such as `"+10"`, whose prefix detects none, names none: with `"+46…"` and `countryCode="NO"` the field shows SE and `onCountryChange` proposes SE. A value without a prefix, as `raw` or `national` output usually is, is read in `countryCode`, whatever country it was typed in. An uncontrolled number never names a country over `countryCode`: a `defaultValue` with another country's prefix keeps it, in international form beside `countryCode`, and a form reset reads `defaultValue` the same way. A change of `countryCode`, or a `countries` or `metadata` change that resolves it to another country, acts like a picker pick of the number shown before: it clears the digits, unless `preserveOnCountryChange` keeps them, and proposes the result through `onChange`. A controlled value is read as it stands in the new country, and the pick is proposed over it. A value that names a country keeps it instead. A `countries`, `metadata` or `autoDetectCountry` change that leaves the controlled country in place is no pick: the number stays, in international form beside `countryCode` when its own country no longer shows, and `onChange` hears nothing. A pick, or a country detected while typing or pasting, is a proposal, which the field shows once the parent sets `countryCode` to it; a parent that keeps its code returns the field to it. Props that show a proposal accept it. A proposal the parent has not answered yet keeps waiting through: - a render with the same props; - a change to `defaultValue`, `defaultCountryCode` or `preserveOnCountryChange` alone; - with `countryCode` set, a change to `outputFormat`, `international`, `formatOnType`, `autoDetectCountry`, `metadata` or `countries` that keeps `value` and `countryCode`, while `countries` still offers the proposal's country: with an uncontrolled number, paste `"+46701234567"` under `countryCode="NO"`, turn on `formatOnType`, then set `countryCode="SE"`, and the paste shows; - an answer to one half of it, which keeps it waiting for the other, in either order: `countryCode` set to its country itself (a code that only falls back to that country is no answer), or a `value` that is its number in a countryless form of the parent's own, such as national digits. Either answer may come with the changes above. A proposal the parent has answered in full ends, as does one whose number the parent holds while the value names another country, which the field shows and `onCountryChange` then proposes. Any other change drops it: a `value` that is not its number in such a form (one with its own `+` or `00` prefix answers for itself), a `countryCode` set to another country, which is a pick of its own, removing `value` or `countryCode`, a `countries` list without its country, and, without `countryCode`, any change but those to the defaults above. Each proposal reaches `onChange` once, whatever order the parent answers in. With a controlled `value`, `onChange` proposes the pick's number at once, and a value the parent accepts without the country is read in `countryCode`, unless it names the picked country itself. With an uncontrolled number, `onChange` reports the pick's number only once the field shows it, so a rejected pick reports nothing. A code the picker does not offer resolves as `defaultCountryCode` does, and `onCountryChange` proposes the country shown. Removing `countryCode` keeps the country and number the field shows. Omit for an uncontrolled country.

props.name: defaultCountryCode
props.description: Initial country. Must be a libphonenumber country with a packaged flag asset. A code the picker does not offer (outside `countries`, excluded, or untyped) falls back to `NO` when offered, else the first offered country in catalog order. Ignored while `countryCode` is set.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial number of an uncontrolled field, read on mount as `value` is. A native form reset restores it, read again under the current props, and calls `onCountryChange` when that changes the country; `""` restores an empty number in `defaultCountryCode`. Without a `defaultValue`, a reset clears the digits and keeps the country. A later change leaves the shown number alone and becomes the next reset's target. Ignored while `value` is set, even to `""`.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Custom/trimmed metadata. Replacement reconciles the picker while preserving existing international identity. A shallow copy, such as `{ ...metadata }` written in a render, is the same metadata and replaces nothing. To limit the picker, pass `countries` instead: trimmed metadata can no longer parse the numbers it leaves out. It does not make the bundle smaller: the field imports its full default metadata either way.

props.name: name
props.description: Hidden input gets `name`; the visible input gets `${name}-display-value`. Unset, neither input submits. Inside a `Form`, the field shows `errors[name]`, clears it when the number it submits changes, and gives `onFormSubmit` that number under `name`, in `outputFormat`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Proposes a formatted output value. Controlled fields display it after parent acceptance. Called only when the proposal differs from the value the parent holds: `value`, compared exactly, or the output an uncontrolled field already shows. So deleting a separator, which keeps the number, calls nothing, while a parent that stores another form of the number, such as national digits, hears every proposal. Also called once as hydration commits, with a number typed or autofilled before the client scripts attached, under the same rule; a controlled parent accepts or rejects it like any other proposal.

props.name: onCountryChange
props.description: Called when the selected picker country changes. With `countryCode` set, called instead for each disagreement, once, as it starts. A disagreement is the field's current country, that of a proposal waiting for the parent, else the one shown, differing from `countryCode`, and is identified by that pair. It continues while the pair holds, as when the parent's props show the waiting proposal; it ends when the current country is `countryCode` again or another country, when `countryCode` changes, or when the parent's next props drop the waiting proposal by not showing its country. So a code the parent just set is never announced, and a disagreement that starts again is announced again. A proposal that moves the country calls `onCountryChange` before `onChange`, so a parent that takes both at once reads the number in the new country.

props.name: preserveOnCountryChange
